MONTHLY PRINCIPAL CHECKLIST

Six checks for October.

Do this as part of an existing leadership meeting. Do not create another meeting just for Title I.

1

Program

Are Title I services, staffing, schedules, frequency, and intensity being delivered as planned?

2

Scholars

Are the intended scholars receiving the support? Which groups are not being reached as planned?

3

Spending

Do upcoming purchases clearly connect to the identified need and the work that was submitted?

4

Coding

Are the function/object codes tied to the purpose of the activity? Use the GRPS Function Code Finder when needed.

5

Families + Evidence

Is the Annual Meeting complete, useful to families, and supported by invitations, agendas, participation, materials, feedback, and access evidence?

6

Adjust

If something is not happening as planned, name the issue, one owner, the correction, due date, and follow-up.

CONTINUEThe work is happening as planned.
CORRECTFix the implementation issue now.
ESCALATEBring forward only what exceeds building authority.

GRPS · ANNUAL TITLE I MEETING

Make the meeting useful to families—and keep the full evidence packet.

GRPS planning reference: complete the Annual Title I Meeting by October 15, 2026. Confirm current MDE/GRPS direction before release. Offer repeat or accessible participation options when needed.

WHAT FAMILIES SHOULD LEAVE KNOWING

Connect Title I to their school and their scholar.

The meeting should answer: What is Title I? What is our school working on? How are Title I resources supporting the work? How will families know whether it is helping? How can families provide input?

Try asking:

“What is one thing that would make it easier for your child to be successful this year?”

Capture the response and document what happens next.

REQUIRED CONTENT

Eight things to cover.

Do not turn this into eight separate presentations. Build one clear conversation that covers the required information.

01

Title I purpose + school program model

What Title I is and how the school uses it.

KEEP:Invitation, agenda, presentation/materials
02

Curriculum, assessments + progress measures

What scholars are learning and how progress is measured.

KEEP:Materials and examples shared
03

Funding + how Title I supports the program

Connect resources to the school need and submitted work.

KEEP:Approved materials and fiscal/program records
04

Family-engagement policy + compact

Explain commitments and how families helped shape them.

KEEP:Policy, compact, input and distribution record
05

School data + improvement priorities

Share the needs and priorities driving the school work.

KEEP:School data, discussion notes and decisions
06

Staff qualifications + required notices

Cover right-to-know and other required information.

KEEP:Notices and distribution evidence
07

Family questions, recommendations + input

Create space for real two-way input.

KEEP:Minutes, feedback, response and follow-up
08

Access supports + participation options

Make participation realistic for families.

KEEP:Translation/interpretation, repeated sessions, disability access and follow-up
GRPS PLANNING PATH

Plan → Hold → Close the loop.

The meeting is not complete when the presentation ends. Close out the evidence and family follow-up.

1

Before the meeting

Set the date, invite families, plan language/access supports, prepare school-specific data, and have the policy/compact ready.

2

During the meeting

Use plain language, connect Title I to school priorities, gather family input, and document questions or recommendations.

3

After the meeting

Distribute the final policy/compact in accessible formats, respond to family input, and file the evidence packet.

4

Follow-up

Do not let the Annual Meeting become the only family engagement. Plan the next learning-linked, two-way opportunity.

GRPS FUNDING + CODING

Need first. Funding second. Coding after that.

Do not start with the item you want to buy. Start with the identified need and the approved work in the Title I plan. Then determine allowability, funding, coding, approval and evidence.

01NeedWhat documented scholar/program need are we addressing?
02PlanWhere is the strategy/activity reflected in the approved plan?
03SupportWhat purchase, service or activity is actually needed?
04Allowability + FundingCan Title I appropriately support it under current guidance?
05Coding + ApprovalVerify fund, function, object/account coding and required approvals.
06Evidence + ResultsKeep the approval/use evidence and review whether it helped.

TITLE I PURCHASE PRE-CHECK

Seven checks before the request moves forward.

A “yes” to all seven does not itself authorize the purchase. Current GRPS approval and current MDE/federal allowability still govern.

1

Need

What documented scholar/program need does this address?

2

Plan alignment

Where is the strategy/activity reflected in the approved MICIP/school plan or Title I program design?

3

Allowability

Is the cost permitted under current Title I guidance?

4

Necessary + reasonable

Is the quantity, quality, timing and price defensible?

5

Program purpose

Can GRPS explain why Title I—not a required general operating obligation—is paying?

6

Coding

Are fund, function, object and account coding confirmed?

7

Evidence

What will be retained to show approval, purchase, delivery/use and program purpose?

GRPS FUNCTION CODE FINDER

Code the purpose of the activity.

  1. Choose the type of activity in the first dropdown.
  2. Choose the best fit from the second dropdown.
  3. Review the code, name, GRPS example and next step.
  4. Then verify the object code and that the funding source allows the expense.

If unsure: choose Not Sure / Other. Do not guess.

ATTACH TO THE REQUEST

Make the rationale easy to follow.

  • Rationale tied to the identified need and approved plan
  • Quote, invoice, cart or other cost detail
  • Required pre-authorization/approval
  • Correct account/coding information
  • Agenda/participant/evaluation documentation when applicable

STOP + ESCALATE BEFORE PURCHASE

Do not guess on higher-risk expenses.

Escalate when the request involves incentives/rewards, food, travel, equipment, construction/facility-type costs, contracts, unusual staffing, or any expense not clearly covered by current guidance.
